name: Estonian

ancestors.notes: Finnish is the closest sister language (mutual Finnic features).
Middle Low German adstrate: the dominant contact layer under the Baltic-German nobility.

notes: Estonian, Finnic language with three phonemic quantity degrees (short, long, overlong). Loanword consonants b, d, g are phonemically lenis (partially voiced). Vowel õ /ɤ/ is typologically unusual. No grammatical gender.

sources.author: Asu, Eva Liina & Teras, Pire
sources.title: Estonian
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Phonetic Association 39(3), 367-372
sources.notes: JIPA Illustration of the IPA. Confirmed via Crossref metadata (DOI 10.1017/S002510030999017X) as the peer-reviewed source for the three phonemic quantity degrees, the lenis (partially voiced) status of loanword b/d/g and the vowel inventory including /ɤ/ (written õ) that this spec's notes describe; the article text itself was not retrieved, so page-level claims here are not independently verified beyond the abstract.

stress.notes: Estonian has categorical initial stress in most words. Vowel and consonant length (degrees Q1/Q2/Q3) are orthographically indicated by geminates. Source: Viitso (1998), Estonian; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonian_phonology
